title: Best Sellers (book sales leaderboard)
description_html:
We are building a system that tracks book sales and updates a leaderboard of best-selling books.

First, decide how to store the current state of book sales. Next, implement an update function that takes in new sales records, updates the current state, and returns a list of the K top-selling titles.

List<string> bestSellers(Map<string, int> sales, Integer k)

Examples

// initial state: empty
bestSellers({"a":  5, "b": 10, "c": 15}, 2) → ["c", "b"]
// state now: { a:  5, b: 10, c: 15 }

bestSellers({"a": 20, "b": 20, "c":  5}, 2) → ["b", "a"]
// state now: { a: 25, b: 30, c: 20 }    (so b=30, a=25 are top 2)

Approach hint

  1. Simple: HashMap<title, int> of cumulative sales. On each call, merge the delta map, then sort entries by total desc and return top K. O(N log N) per query.
  2. Faster query: maintain a min-heap of size K over titles by current total — but updates make heap entries stale; mark stale entries and skip when popping (lazy invalidation).
  3. Fastest with frequent updates: bucket structure modeled on LFU Cache — doubly-linked list of buckets (count → set-of-titles) + HashMap<title, bucket>. update moves the title to the bucket with oldCount + delta; top K walks buckets from the highest count. O(1) per update, O(K) per query.

Tie-breaking, ordering of equal-count titles, and reset semantics should be clarified with the interviewer.

Closest LC patterns: LC 1244 (Design A Leaderboard — premium, literal API match), LC 460 (LFU Cache — closest non-premium for the bucketed-count data structure), LC 432 (All O\'one Data Structure — premium, O(1) inc/dec/max/min), LC 347 / 692 (Top K Frequent — top-K from a counter, simpler one-shot version), LC 703 (Kth Largest in a Stream — streaming Kth).
